name: Gwen Evans
life: “My first shop had a changing screen made from a striped duvet.” On Wednesday, near Juniper Street, Gwen knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I promised free alterations for life in my first advert. This is the first customer to hold me to it.
appearance: Gwen has a long silver braid, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Gwen squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To honor an old alterations promise without charging the new bride twice.
family: Tali James is Gwen’s cousin’s child. Gwen remembers the birthdays. Tali asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The ladder crossing*, Tali says, “I recognized the painter from the night school I quit.”
connections: Cian Reese. They bring the lifetime fitting promise to the customer's chair.

reactions.situation: The bride wants to keep the old pocket
reactions.response: Gwen leaves the pocket in place while the bride tries the dress on.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Gwen repeats the correct name quietly, making the correction easy to hear without turning it into a performance.

reactions.situation: If a stranger returns something damaged
reactions.response: Gwen listens first to the account of how it was actually used.
